v: Probably the first FAMILY movie that you absolutely cannot watch with your family 😉 — a mad Vanga experience swinging from WOW to WTF, DELIGHT to DISGUST, and never playing safe.
e: ANIMAL is less a conventional movie and more an intentionally extreme experience: violent, vulgar, technically polished, frequently excessive and impossible to react to with a single emotion. Ranbir is phenomenal, the BGM and cinematography elevate the madness, and Sandeep Reddy Vanga goes far beyond anything he attempted in Arjun Reddy.
body:
Sandeep Reddy Vanga is probably the first director in the history of world cinema to make a family movie that cannot be watched with family 😉

Rajamouli was absolutely right when he compared Sandeep Reddy Vanga to this generation’s Ram Gopal Varma. ANIMAL feels at least 10X of what Arjun Reddy was — in almost every possible way 🙏

If you are a traditional film lover, one of those intellectuals who immediately asks how a single person can bash hundreds of people, a viewer who cannot handle vulgar actions and dialogues on screen, or someone who expects every character to behave according to conventional morality... then this movie may simply not be for you. Please don’t waste your time 😄

This is not a movie that can be processed like a regular commercial film. For me, it is an EXPERIENCE where the WOW moments and the “what the fuck?” moments come in almost equal quantity.

In some portions you sympathise with the lead character; in others you hate him to the core. In a few scenes you admire how brilliantly something has been portrayed; in others you feel it has been dragged endlessly 🙏

All in all, it is a movie of wildly mixed emotions — taking you from DELIGHT to DISGUST, from WOW to YUCK!!!

Starting with the technical side, the title ANIMAL could not have been more appropriate. The BGM and cinematography are designed extremely well and constantly enhance the visual and audio experience of whatever madness is being unleashed on screen.

Acting-wise, I had very little doubt about who would dominate the awards conversation that season: Ranbir Kapoor. He completely owns this character.

Anil Kapoor does a terrific job as the father, and I was pleasantly surprised by both the characterisation and performance of Rashmika. If there is one genuinely sensible character inside this otherwise crazy world, it is Geetanjali — and Rashmika plays her very well 🙏

The rest of the cast also does its job effectively. Bobby Deol is almost a special appearance in a film running well over three hours, but even with limited screen time he creates a strong impact.

After Kabir Singh — the Hindi version of Arjun Reddy — Sandeep openly said in interviews that he was irritated by reviewers calling that movie “violent” and that one day he would show them what actual violence looks like.

Well... message received 😅

I am still in a trance wondering why and how he decided to use a family backdrop to unleash this level of mad violence. Whatever you think about the choices, the man is definitely a content creator with IRON BALLS 🙏

v: I bow down to Ajay Bhupathi and his team 🙏 — BOLD, RAW, RUSTIC and technically stunning, with the guts to slap society’s hypocrisy right in the face.
e: MANGALAVAARAM impressed me with both its courage and its craft. Ajay Bhupathi tackles physically and emotionally disturbing material without playing safe, Payal Rajput gives an exhausting committed performance, and the cinematography and Ajaneesh Loknath’s BGM turn the thriller into a haunting audiovisual experience.
body:
I bow down to the brilliance of Ajay Bhupathi and his team 🙏

I never expected such an out-and-out BOLD, RAW & RUSTIC Telugu movie — one that throws a direct slap in the face of a hypocritical society and delivers a simple but important message: instead of judging a book by its cover, maybe we should first understand what a person is going through physically and mentally.

It takes serious guts to write a story like this and execute it close to perfection.

And it takes equally serious guts for an actor to accept such a bold, emotionally exhausting role without worrying about where their career currently stands. Hats off to Payal Rajput for completely surrendering herself to the character 🫡

Dasaradhi Sivendra’s cinematography is top-notch. Honestly, a huge number of frames look wallpaper-worthy 😍 The low-light sequences in particular are beautifully shot and add enormously to the mood.

Music and BGM by Ajaneesh Loknath are the soul of this thriller. At its best, the score can give even Anirudh’s elevation BGM a run for its money.

And when I later realised that Ajaneesh was also the music director of Kantara, suddenly none of that quality surprised me 😍

Every character contributes effectively to the thriller atmosphere. Special shout-out to Ajay Ghosh — he was awesome 👍

Having praised all of that, I need to add one very clear warning.

This is a strict NO for sensitive viewers who cannot handle gut-wrenching emotions connected to sexual and physical abuse. The film does not make that material easy to watch.

If those subjects are personally difficult for you, it is genuinely better to skip this movie. Some of the visuals and emotions can stay with you and haunt you long after the film ends 😞

v: Kabhi Eid... Kabhi Diwali... BHAI ke movie bina festival hai AADHURI 😉 A good Salman film after ages, even if Bollywood’s endless spy-universe overdose keeps it only a decent watch for me.
e: Tiger 3 finally gives Salman Khan a solid commercial film again. The story is wafer-thin and YRF’s Pakistan obsession is exhausting, but Salman-Katrina chemistry, entertaining action and the franchise’s continued respect for its female lead make it a decent spy entertainer.
body:
Kabhi Eid... Kabhi Diwali...

BHAI ke movie bina festival hai AADHURI 😉😉

A good Salman Khan film after ages 🙏🙏🙏🙏 — which, for me, makes Tiger 3 a decent watch.

And when I say “decent”, part of that lukewarm reaction is simply because Bollywood has already overloaded us with so many spy thrillers.

When it comes to Bollywood spy films — and especially Yash Raj’s Spy Universe — I genuinely don’t understand the endless obsession with Pakistan.

Tiger 3 takes that obsession one level higher by having an Indian RAW agent effectively trying to protect democracy in Pakistan 🙏

On paper it sounds completely over-the-top, but then... anything is possible with Salman Bhai 😂 And surprisingly, at least while watching the film, I found myself accepting it.

I sincerely hope this is the last Spy Universe movie that revolves so heavily around Pakistan 🙏

One thing I have always liked about the Tiger franchise is that it was among the first fully commercial top-star franchises to give real importance to the female lead instead of using her as decoration.

Good to see that they continue doing that here. Katrina’s Zoya still matters to the story and the action.

Like almost every other spy movie, the core storyline is wafer-thin and has plenty of flaws. But the action sequences and the chemistry between the actors compensate enough to make it a good watch — even if I wouldn’t call it a must-watch.

For people comparing the craze of Tiger 3 with Pathaan, I would remind them that a huge part of Pathaan’s excitement came from SRK doing a full-fledged spy-action film for the first time.

I genuinely wonder whether a Pathaan sequel — if and when it comes — can recreate the same frenzy.

Salman, meanwhile, is doing this effortlessly even in the third Tiger instalment. That shows the command he still has over the masses.

All he really needs to do is bend his back a little and select better scripts... but a serious NO TO TUBELIGHT please 😉😂

The one proper disappointment for me is the music. Forget comparing it with Pathaan — even the first two Tiger films had much peppier and more memorable songs.

The songs here? 😏

v: Nolan gaadi movies decode cheyatam kaadhu raaa... meeku dammunte maa Boyaaa anna SKANDA decode cheyandi 🙏🤣 Ram’s looks and the dances survive; almost everything else is unbearable.
e: SKANDA lost me from the very first scene and never found a way back. A hero introduced as a foreign-university topper and ethical hacker solves everything by flexing muscles, the action becomes parody-level excess, and Thaman’s usually helpful BGM only amplifies the chaos.
body:
Nolan gaadi movies decode cheyatam kaadhu raaa... meeku dammunte maa Boyaaa anna SKANDA decode cheyandi 🙏🙏🙏🤣

This is what happens when filmmakers start assuming their audience has absolutely no sense.

I completely agree that plenty of illogical mass-masala films have become blockbusters. But the successful ones usually grab your attention through at least one department — comedy, emotion, heroism, music, action, something — strongly enough that you voluntarily forget the logic and enjoy what is being shown.

Unfortunately, SKANDA disconnected me right from the first scene itself. After that, I never found a reason to reconnect either with the movie or with its plot.

When you establish your hero as a foreign-university topper and an outstanding ethical hacker, the bare minimum expectation is that at some point he may use his INTELLIGENCE to corner the villains — who, in this case, happen to include the Chief Ministers of two states 🤣😉

But... BUT... BUT...

That would apparently be Nolan’s way of filmmaking.

In Boya’s universe, the hero simply flexes his muscles and solves everything with physical power. That’s it 🙏

Some of the action sequences looked as if they were choreographed by Mutton Kottu Masthan 🤣

Normally, Thaman has this wonderful ability to take an ordinary scene and lift it to the next level with his BGM.

Ironically, that becomes a huge minus here. The scenes are already so ridiculously over-the-top that adding Thaman’s high-energy score pushes them from excessive to almost unbearable 🫡

Taking-wise, the movie is shot in classic Boyapati style: the screen is packed with hundreds of character artists whose primary job is to dress loudly, make exaggerated expressions and deliver over-the-top dialogues praising either the hero or the villain 🙏

For me, the only real positives are Ram’s looks and the Ram-Sreeleela dance combinations.

Except for those two things... almost everything else was unbearable.
